question: Every day that passes brings proof that the Prespa Agreement is a nationally degrading act at Greece’s expense. This shameful agreement, which was imposed on the Greek people by force despite their fierce resistance, not only did not solve a single problem but threw the door wide open to new and dangerous claims by Skopje.

Not only do they continue to use symbols and names that give a further boost to irredentist tendencies, they also stubbornly refuse to correct the gross historical falsifications in their school textbooks, thereby poisoning the minds of future generations with lies and hatred for Greece.

What is most infuriating is that they are systematically and strategically violating an agreement, even though the Syriza government, deplorably, handed a language and a nationality over to them. In light of the above: 1.
Following the reported violations, can consideration to be given to abrogating the Prespa Agreement, damaging as it is to Greece?
How much longer will the EU acquiesce in the promotion of a sham national identity based on stolen elements of Greek culture and the usurpation of Greek history?

Following the above, does the Commission intend to officially suspend all accession negotiations until there is full compliance on their side with European values and their international obligations towards Greece?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.1.2025) The Prespa Agreement is a bilateral treaty between North Macedonia and Greece. As such, it is binding under international law. The agreement sets an example of reconciliation for the region and beyond. To date, both parties have publicly confirmed their commitment to abide by the Agreement.

As recalled in the December 2023 Council Conclusions1 and in the Commission’s 2024 enlargement report on North Macedonia2, the Prespa Agreement needs to be implemented in good faith by all parties. Good neighbourly relations and regional cooperation remain essential elements of the enlargement process.
The Commission will continue to call for adherence to such principles and reiterate the importance of implementing bilateral agreements.
